qc_mont_du_gros_bras.blurb: Mont du Gros-Bras is a winter-only cliff in the Grands-Jardins part of Charlevoix, climbed in a long-day, adventure style. Mixed lines outnumber water ice here: seven mixed routes run from roughly M4 to M7, and four ice lines sit around WI3 to WI4, with several going to multiple pitches. Protection is mostly natural gear, bolts are scarce and there is no fixed rappel line, so parties usually finish by walking off. Faces include a tall north wall on the eastern side of the park. Expect a steep, brushy hike in, and plan for cold, committing days.

qc_c_le_mur_des_larmes.blurb: Le mur des larmes is a sector of the Lac Castor cliff in the Contreforts area of Lanaudiere. Eleven routes, nine of them bolted sport lines and two trad, cover a wide spread from easy fifth-class climbing through the 5.10s and 5.11s up to a single low 5.12, so there is something for most leaders. The cliff overlooks a small lake and faces south, with good summer shade, but it can take a while to dry after rain.

qc_a_secteur_de_gauche.blurb: Secteur de gauche is the first section you meet at the Lac Castor cliff in the Contreforts of Lanaudiere, and it is the hard end of the crag. Of its ten routes, nine are sport and one is trad, and the grades start around 5.10 and then bunch up in the low to mid 5.12s with a couple of 5.13s. The wall catches sun for most of the day, which suits cooler weather, while belayers tend to stand in shade.

qc_c_pain_de_sucre.blurb: Pain de sucre is one of the three crags in the Dame de Coeur area near Val-David in the Laurentides. It holds ten routes, seven sport and three trad, spread from easy 5.7s through a solid block of 5.10 and 5.11 to a few at 5.12 and 5.13. The area's rock is anorthosite, known for good friction and holds in odd shapes and angles. The wall sits a short way beyond the neighbouring crag along the trail.

qc_08_la_renvers_e.blurb: La renversée is the eighth sector of L'Amphitheatre, a quartzite sport-climbing site near Saint-Andre-de-Kamouraska in the Bas-Saint-Laurent. Its ten bolted routes run from very easy climbing up to 5.12, with a cluster in the 5.11 range and a couple of moderates around 5.9, so it suits mixed groups. It is a busy sector, reached by following the main trail past a neighbouring wall, and it looks out over the St. Lawrence River.

qc_f_psy.blurb: PSY is the far-right sector of the small urban climbing spot on Ile Sainte-Helene in Montreal, facing the Stewart Museum. It has the tallest walls on the site, which gives a bit more height than the other sectors. Ten lines split evenly between bouldering and top-rope: boulder problems run from V0 up to V2, and the short top-rope lines are mostly easy to moderate, with a single harder one. It is a handy place to learn outdoor movement and rope skills close to the city.
